Prepare session to perform analyses
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)

```

Read-in store sales data file, save as R object, and parse as needed
```{r}
# here is the initial code to read-in the store sales data and save it as an R object
store_data <- read_excel("US Superstore data.xls")

# after saving, I'll print once to get an idea of how the object saved and what parsing needs to take place to perform further analysis
store_data
class(store_data)

# the object was initially read-in as a tibble, so I don't need to make any conversions in order to work with it in the tidyverse.  Now, I'll parse the data as needed.
store_data |>
  rename("Row_ID" = "Row ID",
         "Order_ID" = "Order ID",
         "Order_Date" = "Order Date",
         "Ship_Date" = "Ship Date",
         "Ship_Mode" = "Ship Mode",
         "Customer_ID" = "Customer ID",
         "Customer_Name" = "Customer Name",
         "Postal_Code" = "Postal Code",
         "Sub_Category" = "Sub-Category",
         "Product_ID" = "Product ID",
         "Product_Name" = "Product Name"
         ) |>
  mutate(
    Order_Date = as.Date(Order_Date),
    Ship_Date = as.Date(Ship_Date),
    Ship_Mode = as.factor(Ship_Mode),
    Segment = as.factor(Segment),
    State = as.factor(State),
    Postal_Code = as.character(Postal_Code),
    Region = as.factor(Region),
    Category = as.factor(Category),
    Sub_Category = as.factor(Sub_Category)
  )

```
